ranking_by: maximum wingspan of living flying birds, in feet
title: The 5 Widest Bird Wingspans Alive, Ranked (#1 Beats a Small Car)

scenes.text: A condor doesn't win. Number one has wings wider than a small car is long.
Number five: the marabou stork. Over ten feet from wingtip to wingtip, on a bird that scavenges.
scenes.label: Marabou stork · 10.5 ft

scenes.text: Number four: the Andean condor. Close to eleven feet, and it can soar for hours.
scenes.label: Andean condor · 10.8 ft

scenes.text: Number three: the Dalmatian pelican. About eleven and a half feet, the largest pelican in Europe.
scenes.label: Dalmatian pelican · 11.5 ft

scenes.text: Number two: the great white pelican. Almost twelve feet across, and it can still take off from water.
scenes.label: Great white pelican · 11.8 ft

scenes.text: Number one: the wandering albatross. About twelve feet, and it glides over the ocean for months.
scenes.label: Wandering albatross · 12 ft

description:
The five widest wingspans of any living flying bird, ranked by maximum wingspan.
Sources differ by a few inches, so the figures are approximate, but the order holds.
Which bird would you put at number one?
first_comment: Did the albatross surprise you? Which animal list should we rank next?
